as_of_line: As of 17:45 Prague time, 2 November. The statuses update as the work moves.
headline: What's being built today
intro: Fourteen pieces of work (one since retired), run by AI agents working in parallel, with Alex steering. First comes the tooling that lets the agents work on their own. Then come the demos of what a GTM engineer builds, and they all end up on this site.

how_it_runs.text: Alex wrote a project charter in the morning: the goal, the rules every agent follows, and the list of deliverables.

how_it_runs.lead: One agent per piece of work.
how_it_runs.text: Each deliverable gets its own spec, a plan an agent can carry out on its own, and its own background Claude Code session. The sessions run at the same time and message each other.
Any agent that needs Alex sends its question to the "answer desk", a single window that shows him one question at a time.
Anything that needs Alex (recordings, decisions, sign-offs) happens while he's at the computer today. The rest builds overnight, and a cleanup session follows tomorrow morning.

tooling.what: Sets up a working folder, instructions and a background session for every other piece.
Decides with Alex what gets researched and how deep, so the agents work from findings instead of guesses.
tooling.status: Done. The research for the blog, Canva and LinkedIn demos is in. Alex dropped the last two lists at 17:03.

tooling.what: Keeps the plan consistent: adds deliverables and updates everything that depends on them.
tooling.status: The charter now matches Alex's latest calls (17:10): 36 workflows, two blog posts, the blog pipeline retired.

demos.demo: Scraping and research on the Apify API
demos.what: Scraping and researching prospects at scale on the Apify API. It goes first, because other demos use what it finds.
demos.status: Signed off by Alex at 17:14, with one change: the research it produced goes first, as a carousel. Being built.

demos.what: Deep research on the company and the people likely to be involved in hiring.
demos.status: Alex's own research, with no agent session of its own. First pass done at about 15:34. It feeds the outbound, scraping, brand and website work.

demos.what: Two short demos, each a video with a summary to read. First, classification tools and the 36 outbound workflows in GetSales: four customer profiles, in English, Czech and German, with three approaches each, every one opening with a first message written for its lead. Second, a screen capture of sorting people into customer profiles. Nothing sends.
demos.status: All 36 workflows built by 17:34, switched off, with no leads. Next, Alex records two short demos.

demos.what: Was meant to turn 15 minutes of Alex talking into a near-finished blog post.
demos.status: Retired by Alex at 16:45: the posts are the deliverable, not a separate pipeline. Its tools went to demo 5.

demos.what: Two posts on the ideas behind this project, each from 15 minutes of Alex talking, brought to near-final. He writes the last 10%.
demos.status: Topics set by Alex. A research base for each article is ready. Next, Alex dictates them.

demos.what: Pixel-perfect, on-brand visual templates for LinkedIn.
demos.status: Five templates built and checked. With Alex for his brand sign-off since 17:42, then into Canva.

demos.what: LinkedIn posts written in the company's own voice.
demos.status: Five posts written in the company's voice. A blind judge scored each 21 out of 21. Next, Alex's brand sign-off.

demos.what: A page for each key stakeholder, and a running picture of the project.
demos.status: Live in the company's look since 16:29, with a page per demo.

demos.what: An agent that watches the recordings and tells the website what to add. This section is its first post.
demos.status: Running. Its plan was approved at 17:03.

demos.what: Alex designing in Canva, on camera, near the end of the day.
demos.status: Filming tonight, once the templates are in Canva.

demos.what: Video generation giving the brand some energy: a 5-second animation of one Addvery LinkedIn graphic, and a one-minute brand video. Alex makes both with Comfy.
demos.status: Added at 17:30. Ideas first, for Alex to pick from.

after_how_it_runs.text: Think of it like the expensive movie actor. They fly him out to the scene, they shoot all of his scenes first, even if it's not in chronological order of the movie, because his time is the most expensive.
after_how_it_runs.source: Alex, S03 at 11:11 (11:36 Prague), on why everything that needs him is done first

after_demos.text: Without being prompted, it should see all this stuff being built and say, okay, these are the deliverables. Let's find a way to put the deliverables on the website so people kind of know what to expect.
after_demos.source: Alex, S04 at 08:23 (12:24 Prague), describing the legibility analyzer
